migration.migration_reason: Historical paid Semantic Compression evidence was re-adjudicated against the current frozen rubric by the trusted GPT-5.6 Sol recertifier. The result is bound to a frozen provenance snapshot containing the exact legacy source hashes and current canonical fragments. This mode never claims that legacy fragments were mechanically compiled when the retained run did not perform that verification.

F01.P1.justification: const n = 7; return n; — non-reassignable binding.

F01.P2.fragment:
let counter: number = 0;
const LIMIT: number = 100;
F01.P2.justification: let counter: bigint = 0n; const LIMIT: bigint = 100n; BigInt covers full 64-bit signed range and beyond.

F02.P1.justification: let v: number; declared without initializer; TS definite-assignment analysis accepts both-branch assignment before read under --strict.

F02.P2.justification: JS/TS ArrayBuffer/TypedArray storage is spec-guaranteed zero-initialized; no documented mechanism yields genuinely uninitialized bulk storage. Per R9 named substitution, wrote default-initialized Uint8Array(16) fragment instead; substitute is never FULL.

F03.P1.justification: x += 1; in-place compound assignment on primitive local.

F03.P2.justification: xs[1] = 42; in-place element mutation of Array, no rebind.

F04.P1.justification: JS/TS has no documented mechanism for a second name to alias and write the same scalar primitive local (no pointers/references/inout for primitives); object-wrapper substitution is explicitly not an acceptable substitute for FULL and this probe carries no R9 exception, so NONE is recorded per N-4.

F04.P2.fragment:
const window: ReadonlyArray<number> = xs;
return window[0];
F04.P2.justification: const window: ReadonlyArray<number> = xs; — same underlying reference (no element copy), TS compiler forbids mutation through the readonly-typed view; documented TS readonly-array typing mechanism.

F04.P3.justification: Route `first` through a one-element array and read back as `second`; `same = (first === second)` uses standard JS reference-equality operator, distinct from structural/value equality.

F05.P1.justification: f(x) bare call; JS/TS arrays are reference-semantic objects passed by reference by default at ordinary call sites.

F05.P2.justification: Canonical task explicitly directs NONE for languages lacking a documented mechanism for a callee to write a caller's scalar local; JS/TS has no pass-by-reference/pointer/inout for primitives.

F05.P3.justification: const neg = (a: number) => k - a; const ys = xs.map(neg); closure captures k, neg referred to by name at the map call.

F06.P1.justification: function mid(a:number[]):number{return a[1];} numbers are primitive value type in JS, y is independent of xs.

F06.P2.justification: TS tuple type [number,number] returned from divmod2, destructured as const [q,r] = divmod2(a,b);

F07.P1.justification: const r = a * b + c; ordinary operator precedence.

F07.P2.justification: const q = Math.trunc(a / b); const m = a % b; const d = a / b; (JS numbers are float64 so real division is the plain operator; Math.trunc is the standard truncating-integer-division form).

F08.P1.justification: TypeScript/JavaScript number is IEEE-754 binary64 rather than a signed 32-bit integer type. ToInt32 coercion through a bitwise operator is a conversion substitute for the required fixed-width binding, and F08.P1 has no R9 substitution. The prior FULL/P-a interpretations are therefore NONE under the current rubric.

F08.P2.justification: const q = (b === 0) ? 0 : Math.trunc(a / b); — explicit guard (rung ii), since no standard checked-division optional-returning operation exists in JS.

F09.P1.justification: const eq = (s1 === s2); JS strings are primitives with value semantics so === compares contents.

F09.P2.fragment:
xs.sort((a, b) => b - a);
const lt = a < b;
F09.P2.justification: xs.sort((a,b) => b - a); explicit descending comparator, Array.prototype.sort mutates and returns same reference; const lt = a < b;

F10.P1.justification: const small = Number(big) | 0; — explicit narrowing to 32-bit representation via documented ToInt32 bitwise conversion (rung ii); no checked/optional narrowing op exists in stdlib.

F10.P2.justification: const sum = i + d; JS has one numeric (float64) representation so no distinct conversion syntax is required or possible; fragment still delivers the stated behavior.

F11.P1.justification: const e = xs[i]; return e; ordinary indexed read (out-of-range yields undefined per spec, a support-neutral observation for metrics B/D).

F11.P2.justification: const part = xs.slice(1,4); const v = part[0]; Array.prototype.slice is the standard sub-range form (produces a new array).

F12.P1.justification: let o: number | null = null; const n = o ?? 0; nullish-coalescing is the standard TS/JS optional-fallback form.

F12.P2.justification: JS/TS has optional chaining (?.) for property/method access only, no standard Optional-map operation over an arbitrary function applied to a nullable scalar. Per R9 named substitution wrote the explicit-conditional form; never FULL.

F13.P1.justification: The standard Number/parseInt conversions report malformed input as NaN rather than a propagating failure. Adding an isNaN check handles and manufactures the failure locally, contrary to the canonical requirement to propagate the standard conversion's own failure without handling it. F13.P1 has no R9 substitution.

F13.P2.justification: const parsed = Number(s); const n = Number.isNaN(parsed) ? 0 : parsed; local handling with fallback, ordinary conditional permitted for this probe.

F14.P1.fragment:
type Shape = { kind: "circle"; r: number } | { kind: "rect"; w: number; h: number };
const s: Shape = { kind: "circle", r: 2.0 };
F14.P1.justification: type Shape = {kind:'Circle', r:number} | {kind:'Rect', w:number, h:number}; discriminated union, closed by declaration; const s: Shape = {kind:'Circle', r:2.0};

F14.P2.justification: The retained discriminated-union switch delivers every numbered requirement with no default arm and computes both Circle and Rect areas. Compiler-enforced exhaustiveness is explicitly an OBSERVATION TARGET scored by B/D, not a Capability Coverage support requirement, so the legacy PARTIAL/P-c judgment double-counted determinacy.

F14.P3.justification: interface Shape{area():number;} in shapes.ts with Circle/Rect implementations; a separate file adds class Tri implementing Shape without editing shapes.ts; dispatch through the Shape-typed value calls Tri's area().

F15.P1.justification: function head<T>(xs:T[]):T{return xs[0];} used at number[] and string[] with T recoverable at each call site.

F15.P2.justification: function max_of<T extends number>(a:T,b:T):T{return a>b?a:b;} (or a Comparable-style interface bound) — declaration-site generic constraint.

F15.P3.justification: interface Named{tag():string;} classes A,B implement it; const items: Named[] = [new A(), new B()]; items[0].tag() dispatches at runtime without a[0]'s concrete type being statically recoverable from items' declared type.

F16.P1.justification: const xs=[1,2,3]; const total = xs.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0); standard reduce operation.

F16.P2.justification: const mp = new Map([['a',1]]); for (const [k,v] of mp) total+=v; const miss = mp.get('b') ?? 0; Map iteration order is insertion order per spec; get on missing key returns undefined.

F17.P1.justification: async function readAll(){const fh = await fs.promises.open('data.txt','r'); try {...} finally { await fh.close(); }} try/finally guarantees release on every exit path including failure.

F17.P2.justification: ES2023 'using' declarations with Symbol.dispose would provide a true deterministic end-of-lifetime hook, but require lib.esnext.disposable typings not included under the frozen recipe's default lib for --target es2022 (a P-b flag/lib addition beyond the frozen recipe). Per R9 named substitution, wrote the nearest standard construct instead: an explicit dispose() method invoked via try/finally at the end of an enclosing block, incrementing `released` exactly once; never FULL.

F18.P1.justification: console.log('x'); global standard facility, no import required under Node's default globals.

F18.P2.justification: util.ts: export function pub_add(a,b){return a+b+secret();} function secret(){return 1;} (non-exported, module-private); main.ts: import * as util from './util'; util.pub_add(2,3); module-scoping enforces the boundary.

F19.P1.justification: const [a,b] = await Promise.all([f1(), f2()]); const sum = a+b; async/await plus Promise.all is the standard concurrent-join facility; top-level await is available under --module nodenext.

F19.P2.justification: Two worker_threads each performing 1000 Atomics.add operations on a SharedArrayBuffer-backed Int32Array, joined via worker 'exit' events/promises; Atomics.add is documented by the ECMAScript specification as an atomic read-modify-write, giving a normative race-freedom guarantee; final counter value 2000 verified across 20 runs.

F20.P1.justification: Node/TS ship no built-in FFI mechanism to call an arbitrary C function; reaching abs(int) would require a native addon (node-gyp/N-API) which is a separate build system/toolchain outside the frozen recipe (R7), or a third-party ffi package (forbidden).

F20.P2.justification: tsc/node produce no compiled artifact exposing a C-ABI unmangled symbol under the frozen recipe; no built-in mechanism to export a stable extern-C symbol. nm field: 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe'.
